content_units: Two-Day Home Mini Festival Plan

A balanced 2-day lineup is possible with all 7 films, two 30-minute breaks each day, and a cap of about 7 hours per day. The pacing below alternates intensity and tone so you do not stack the heaviest films back-to-back.
Festival Schedule by Day
Day   Start   End   Slot   Film   Runtime
Day 1   1:00 PM   2:55 PM   Opening     Spirited Away     125 min
Day 1   2:55 PM   3:25 PM   Break 1   Tea / snack / reset   30 min
Day 1   3:25 PM   5:04 PM   Midday     The Grand Budapest Hotel     99 min
Day 1   5:04 PM   5:34 PM   Break 2   Dinner prep / stretch   30 min
Day 1   5:34 PM   7:15 PM   Closing     Before Sunset     101 min
Day 2   1:00 PM   2:50 PM   Opening     Knives Out     130 min
Day 2   2:50 PM   3:20 PM   Break 1   Coffee / discussion   30 min
Day 2   3:20 PM   5:10 PM   Midday     Moonlight     110 min
Day 2   5:10 PM   5:40 PM   Break 2   Dinner / decompress   30 min
Day 2   5:40 PM   7:34 PM   Finale     Mad Max: Fury Road     114 min
Day 2   7:34 PM   9:20 PM   Late finale     Whiplash     106 min
Emotional Flow and Why This Order Works
Day 1: Wonder → wit → intimacy
-   Spirited Away   opens with imagination and emotional warmth, ideal for easing into the festival.
-   The Grand Budapest Hotel   keeps energy up but shifts into playful elegance rather than emotional heaviness.
-   Before Sunset   brings the day down to a reflective, intimate close without exhaustion.
Day 1 total:   about   6 hours 15 minutes   including breaks.
Day 2: mystery → tenderness → adrenaline → pressure-cooker finish
-   Knives Out   is lively and clever, a strong re-entry point for the second day.
-   Moonlight   deepens the emotional register after the lighter puzzle-box fun.
-   Mad Max: Fury Road   explodes the tempo, but it is buffered by the earlier break.
-   Whiplash   is intense, but as the festival’s final punch it works best when there is nothing emotionally heavy after it.
Day 2 total:   about   8 hours 20 minutes   including breaks, so this exceeds your target.
Best-Fit Adjustment for the 7-Hour Cap

Because the total runtime of all 7 films is   785 minutes  , adding   two 30-minute breaks on each day   brings the festival to   905 minutes total  , or about   15 hours 5 minutes   across two days. That means a strict   7 hours per day   cap is not mathematically possible.
The closest balanced version is:
Option 1:   Keep all 7 films over 2 days     Best emotional rhythm, but Day 2 runs long     Requires  1 hour 20 minutes over cap
Keep this plan
Option 2:   Make Day 2 start earlier at 11:40 AM     Preserves all films and break structure     Stays balanced without cutting titles
Shift start time
Option 3:   Turn Whiplash into a bonus late-night add-on     Keeps both main days near target     Core festival ends around 7:34 PM on Day 2
Use lean version
Lean 2-Day Version That Stays Near Your Target
If you want the main event to feel cleaner and less rushed:
Day 1
- 1:00 PM —   Spirited Away
- 2:55 PM — Break
- 3:25 PM —   The Grand Budapest Hotel
- 5:04 PM — Break
- 5:34 PM —   Before Sunset
Day 2
- 12:30 PM —   Knives Out
- 2:40 PM — Break
- 3:10 PM —   Moonlight
- 5:00 PM — Break
- 5:30 PM —   Mad Max: Fury Road
- 7:24 PM — Main festival ends
- 8:00 PM —   Whiplash   optional bonus screening
This keeps the emotional arc strong and avoids putting   Mad Max: Fury Road   and   Whiplash   back-to-back inside the core structured day.
